content: Certainly. 1. Katayama H and Vinjé J (2017) discussed the role of norovirus and other caliciviruses in the context of global waterborne pathogens. Their work is included in the Global Water Pathogens Project, edited by Rose JB and Jiménez-Cisneros B, and published by Michigan State University in collaboration with UNESCO. 2. Khin NO, Sebastian AA, and Aye T (1989) investigated the carriage of enteric bacterial pathogens by houseflies in Yangon, Myanmar. Their findings were published in the Journal of Diarrhoeal Disease Research, highlighting the role of flies in pathogen transmission. 3. Kim JH et al. (2011) explored the correlation between the number of discharged worms and fecal egg counts in human clonorchiasis. Their study, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases, provided insights into the diagnostic and epidemiological aspects of this parasitic infection. 4. Lalloo D and White N (2013) contributed to the 23rd edition of Manson’s Tropical Diseases, a comprehensive reference on tropical infectious diseases, published by Elsevier Saunders. 5. Léger E and Webster JP (2017) examined hybridization events in Schistosoma species and their implications for evolution, epidemiology, and control strategies. Their work was published in Parasitology. 6. Maier RM, Pepper IL, and Gerba CP (2009) authored Environmental Microbiology, a detailed textbook on microbial interactions in environmental systems, published by Academic Press. 7. Mandell GL, Bennett JE, and Dolin R (2009) presented the Principles and Practice of Infectious Diseases, a foundational text in infectious disease management, published by Churchill Livingstone Elsevier. 8. Manser ND et al. (2016) modeled the inactivation of highly persistent pathogens in household-scale semi-continuous anaerobic digesters. Their findings were published in Environmental Engineering Science. 9. Marshall KC (1971) investigated the sorptive interactions between soil particles and microorganisms, contributing to the book Soil Biochemistry, Volume 2, edited by McLaren AD and Skujins J, and published by Marcel Dekker. 10. Meleg E et al. (2008) detected and quantified group C rotaviruses in communal sewage, as reported in Applied and Environmental Microbiology. 11. Murrell KD and Pozio E (2017) reviewed liver flukes, including Clonorchis sinensis, Opisthorchis spp., and Metorchis spp., in the Global Water Pathogens Project, edited by Rose JB and Jiménez-Cisneros B. 12. Nasser AM (2016) reviewed the removal of Cryptosporidium through wastewater treatment processes, with findings published in the Journal of Water and Health. 13. The National Research Council (2004) published Indicators for Waterborne Pathogens, a report by The National Academies Press in Washington, DC. 14. Park W-J et al. (2016) identified hepatitis E virus as an emerging zoonotic pathogen, with their study published in the Journal of Veterinary Science. 15. Petterson SR et al. (2016) proposed a theoretical approach to modeling norovirus concentrations in surface water using fecal indicator data, as applied to the Glomma River in Norway. Their work appeared in Water Research. 16. Pitkänen T and Hanninen ML (2017) reviewed members of the Campylobacteraceae family, including Campylobacter jejuni and Campylobacter coli, in the Global Water Pathogens Project. 17. Rendtorff RC (1954) conducted experimental studies on the transmission of human intestinal protozoan parasites, focusing on Giardia lamblia cysts. The findings were published in the American Journal of Hygiene. 18. Robb K et al. (2017) assessed fecal exposure pathways in low-income urban neighborhoods in Accra, Ghana, as part of the SaniPath study. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. 19. Rudge JW et al. (2013) identified host species driving the transmission of Schistosomiasis japonica in China, a multi-host parasite system. Their study was published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the USA. 20. Schiff GM et al. (1984) studied echovirus-12 in volunteers, determining the minimal infectious dose and the effect of prior infection on susceptibility. Their findings were published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases. 21. Scholz T et al. (2009) provided an update on the human broad tapeworm (genus Diphyllobothrium), including its clinical relevance, in Clinical Microbiology Reviews. 22. Seitz SR et al. (2011) investigated norovirus infectivity in humans and its persistence in water, with results published in Applied and Environmental Microbiology. 23. Sharafi K et al. (2015) compared parasitic contamination in domestic raw wastewater and clinical referrals, as reported in the Research Journal of Environmental Science. 24. Stocks ME et al. (2014) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the effect of water, sanitation, and hygiene interventions on trachoma prevention, published in PLoS Medicine. 25. Szostakowska B et al. (2004) recovered Cryptosporidium parvum and Giardia lamblia from flies on a cattle farm and in a landfill, with findings published in Applied and Environmental Microbiology. 26. Tatfeng YM et al. (2005) examined the mechanical transmission of pathogenic organisms by cockroaches, as reported in the Journal of Vector Borne Diseases. 27. Teunis PF et al. (2008) studied the infectivity of Norwalk virus, with findings published in the Journal of Medical Virology. 28. Teunis PF et al. (2002) conducted dose-response studies on Cryptosporidium, highlighting variations between isolates, as reported in Risk Analysis. 29. Teunis PF et al. (2015) investigated norovirus shedding in symptomatic and asymptomatic infections, with results published in Epidemiology and Infection. 30. Tischendorf J et al. (2016) reviewed the risk of infection following colonization with carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae, as published in the American Journal of Infection Control. 31. Van Abel N et al. (2017) compared risk predictions from multiple norovirus dose-response models, with implications for quantitative microbial risk assessment, as reported in Risk Analysis. 32. Van den Berg H et al. (2013) advocated for integrated vector management in addressing malaria and lymphatic filariasis, as published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases. 33. Van der Poel W and Rzezutka A (2017a) reviewed hepatitis A in the Global Water Pathogens Project. 34. Van der Poel W and Rzezutka A (2017b) reviewed hepatitis E in the Global Water Pathogens Project. 35. Vu D-L et al. (2017) examined the epidemiology of classic and novel human astroviruses, focusing on gastroenteritis and beyond, as published in Viruses. 36. Ward RL et al. (1986) studied human rotavirus in volunteers, determining the infectious dose and serological response, as reported in the Journal of Infectious Diseases. 37. Widerström M et al. (2014) reported a large outbreak of Cryptosporidium hominis infection transmitted through the public water supply in Sweden, as published in Emerging Infectious Diseases. 38. Yates M (2017) provided an overview of pathogen persistence in fecal wastes and wastewater matrices in the Global Water Pathogens Project. 39. The World Health Organization (2016) published guidelines on sanitation and health, detailing methods for guideline development and evidence synthesis. 40. The World Health Organization (undated) provided resources on taeniasis and its management. This version is structured to provide clear, professional descriptions of the studies and their findings, suitable for a medical or scientific audience.
